raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`compute_mamba_state_slice_blocks` (shared by the NIXL, Mooncake and MORI PD backends) slices each GDN conv sub-block (`cat([q | k | v])`) as `full_dim // tp`. That is only correct when the TP size divides the head count. GDN key heads (the q and k rows) are 16 on Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5. At attention TP 32 or 64 they are replicated: rank `r` holds key head `r // (tp // 16)`, which is the layout `Mamba2StateShape.create` sizes via `extra_groups_for_head_shards`. The local q and k sub-blocks are then one head wide, not `key_dim // tp`. The `use_subdims` check (`sum(groups) == src_dim * tp`) fails, and the code falls back to one contiguous slice that straddles q/k/v and delivers the wrong channels. Nothing raises.

This affects any prefill/decode pair where either side's attention TP is larger than the number of key heads.

## Modifications

- `conv_shard_groups` entries may now be `(full_dim, num_heads)` pairs as well as bare full dims.
- `compute_mamba_state_slice_blocks` slices each sub-block on head ranges. It writes the overlap of the prefill rank's heads with the decode rank's heads, and uses the same replication rule as the state shape. In aggregation (prefill TP > decode TP), a replicated head is written only by the first writer of the decode rank.
- A bare full dim is treated as "every channel is a head", which reproduces the previous blocks exactly when the TP sizes divide the dim. The new test checks this.
- `Qwen3NextConfig.mamba2_cache_params` declares `(dim, heads)` for its q/k/v sub-blocks. Behavior is unchanged for TP ≤ 16.

## How it was found

We are writing an out-of-tree Neuron/Trainium platform plugin and serve Qwen3.5 with GDN TP up to 64. A CPU harness compared upstream's slice math with a reference implementation on synthetic GDN states. With bare dims (current behavior), **38 of 66** heterogeneous (prefill TP, decode TP) pairs across three head configurations deliver wrong data or mis-sized blocks. All 38 have TP larger than the key-head count on one side.

Note: as far as I can tell, the in-tree Qwen3-Next model (`num_k_heads // attn_tp_size`) does not run GDN with attention TP > `num_k_heads` today. So the bug is reachable from out-of-tree models and from any future in-tree support. The state-shape helper already handles the replicated case; only PD slicing did not.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run (no GPU). For the in-tree model at TP ≤ 16 the change produces identical blocks (covered by the new test).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This only changes host-side block computation, with the same number of blocks per sub-block.

## Tests

- Run (macOS, CPU only):
  - `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mamba_state_slice_replicated_heads.py` (new). It builds every rank's local conv rows as logical channel ids, applies the blocks for every targeted (prefill, decode) pair over a TP grid up to 64, and checks each decode row is written exactly once with the right channel. It also checks that bare dims == pairs when divisible.
  - `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py`: still passes (65 passed in total).
- Not run: e2e PD with Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 on GPU; MORI/Mooncake/NIXL transfers on hardware.

## Open questions

- Encoding: I extended `conv_shard_groups` entries to optional `(dim, heads)` pairs so the backends pass them through unchanged. The alternative is a parallel `conv_shard_heads` list plumbed through `KVArgs.state_conv_shard_groups` and the three backends. Which do reviewers prefer?
- Should the Kimi linear-attention groups (`[proj_size, proj_k_size, proj_k_size]` in `mamba_utils.py`) also declare head counts?
- Temporal state still assumes TP divides the value-head count (true for all current GDN models).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""CPU tests for GDN conv-state PD slicing when attention TP exceeds key heads.
+
+GDN conv_state is ``cat([q | k | v])``. Value heads divide every TP size, but
+key heads (q and k rows) may not: Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 have 16 key heads, so
+TP 32 or 64 replicates them (rank r holds key head ``r // (tp // 16)``, the
+layout ``Mamba2StateShape.create`` sizes for). The slice used to assume every
+sub-block is ``full_dim // tp`` wide and fell back to one contiguous slice,
+which delivered wrong channels.
+
+Each test builds every rank's local conv rows as logical channel ids, applies
+the blocks from ``compute_mamba_state_slice_blocks`` for every (prefill rank,
+decode rank) pair SGLang targets, and checks the decode rows.
+"""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.utils import compute_mamba_state_slice_blocks
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+def _heads_on_rank(tp, rank, num_heads):
+    if num_heads % tp == 0:
+        per = num_heads // tp
+        return rank * per, per
+    assert tp % num_heads == 0
+    return rank // (tp // num_heads), 1
+
+
+def _local_rows(groups, tp, rank):
+    """Logical channel ids of a rank's conv rows: per sub-block, its heads."""
+    rows, base = [], 0
+    for full_dim, heads in groups:
+        head_dim = full_dim // heads
+        h0, hn = _heads_on_rank(tp, rank, heads)
+        rows.extend(range(base + h0 * head_dim, base + (h0 + hn) * head_dim))
+        base += full_dim
+    return np.asarray(rows)
+
+
+def _targets(p_tp, d_tp, d_rank):
+    if d_tp >= p_tp:
+        return [d_rank // (d_tp // p_tp)]
+    k = p_tp // d_tp
+    return list(range(d_rank * k, (d_rank + 1) * k))
+
+
+def transfer(groups, p_tp, d_tp, shard_groups_arg):
+    for d in range(d_tp):
+        want = _local_rows(groups, d_tp, d)
+        got = np.full_like(want, -1)
+        writes = np.zeros_like(want)
+        for p in _targets(p_tp, d_tp, d):
+            src = _local_rows(groups, p_tp, p)
+            for s0, d0, n in compute_mamba_state_slice_blocks(
+                src_dim=len(src),
+                dst_dim=len(want),
+                src_attn_tp_size=p_tp,
+                dst_attn_tp_size=d_tp,
+                dst_tp_rank_in_group=d,
+                local_tp_rank_in_group=p,

+MODELS = {
+    # (key_dim, n_k), (key_dim, n_k), (value_dim, n_v); head dims shrunk.

+def _tps(groups, candidates):
+    nv = groups[2][1]
+    return [t for t in candidates if nv % t == 0]

+    def test_grid(self):
